title: Preparing for HPC on RISC-V: Examining Vectorization and Distributed Performance of an Astrophysics Application with HPX and Kokkos
problem: Early RISC-V processors with finalized vector specifications require evaluation for HPC suitability. The challenge is porting modern C++ HPC applications to RISC-V and assessing whether variable-length vectorization and vector-chaining capabilities deliver competitive performance compared to established HPC systems.
motivation: RISC-V is gaining mainstream HPC adoption due to energy efficiency concerns, and first commercial RISC-V CPUs with vector support are now available, making viability assessment critical.
method: The paper ports Octo-Tiger, a multi-physics 3D adaptive mesh refinement astrophysics application built on HPX and Kokkos, to RISC-V. The std::experimental::simd interface is implemented to exploit RISC-V Vector extension for variable-length array processing and vector-chaining. Performance, scalability, and power consumption are evaluated on RISC-V single board computers and compared against A64FX systems.
key_novelty: First comprehensive evaluation of RISC-V vector processors for a production-grade HPC application using modern C++ framework abstractions (HPX/Kokkos).
contributions: Successful port of Octo-Tiger astrophysics application to RISC-V with vector extension support
Implementation and integration of std::experimental::simd for RISC-V vectorization
Comparative performance, scalability, and power analysis against A64FX
Viability assessment of RISC-V for real-world HPC workloads
